bibliography.corrections: Give the full citation: Snow, H. E. 1978. A 15-year study of the harvest, exploitation, and mortality of fishes in Murphy Flowage, Wisconsin. Technical Bulletin No. 103. Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Madison. 22 pp.
bibliography.note: author Howard E. Snow; the ledger's '(Murphy Flowage)' stands in for the title

claims.claim: natural A ≈ 55–70 % in two Midwest lakes (Snow 1978; Schneider 1973a) — Snow's part: ~55 %
claims.conditions: Murphy Flowage (180 acres, ~73 ha), 1955–69 averages; natural mortality v (Ricker's notation) 55 % (annual range 28–86), total mortality A 61 % (34–90), angling exploitation u 5 %; from Petersen estimates of fin-clipped fish, perch marked each spring at ≥ 5.0 in (12.7 cm) TL; largemouth bass and northern pike present, muskellunge stocked
total mortality A 72 % (59–87), highest of the panfish; natural 60 %; angling 8 %; pumpkinseed marked at ≥ 4.0 in TL; 1955–69

claims.claim: a Wisconsin flowage drew 182 angler-hours per hectare per year
claims.location: Abstract (PDF p. 3); p. 4 (PDF p. 7), Hours Fished
claims.quote: On the average each year, anglers fished 73.6 hours per acre
claims.conditions: compulsory registration creel census, 30 Apr 1955 – 31 May 1970; 13,242 hours a year on 180 acres
claims.note: 73.6 h/acre × 2.471 = 181.9 h/ha (the project's conversion is right)

claims.claim: the flowage was fished at about the average for north-central waters
claims.conditions: 'could be considered about average as compared to other north central waters but above average when compared to waters in sparsely populated areas'; far below the 567 h/acre of 12 intensively managed Alabama lakes (p. 4)

claims.claim: a Wisconsin flowage open to unlimited harvest
claims.quote: closed fishing season and neither a bag
claims.conditions: 'There was no closed fishing season and neither a bag limit nor size limit was in effect on Murphy Flowage at any time'

claims.claim: angling took only 5 % of yellow perch, 8 % of pumpkinseed and 2 % of brown bullhead a year against natural mortality of 48–60 %; only largemouth exploitation (27 %) exceeded natural mortality
claims.quote: largemouth bass is the only species for
claims.conditions: Table 7: angling u — yellow perch 5, pumpkinseed 8, brown bullhead 2 (natural v 55, 60, 48); largemouth bass u 27 vs v 21 ('the only species for which the rate of exploitation exceeded the natural mortality rate'); northern pike u 26 vs v 40; bullhead marked at ≥ 8.0 in; 1955–69 means

claims.conditions: as above: perch ≥ 5.0 in (12.7 cm) TL, not ≥ 7.5 cm (the paragraph's lead-in size); annual range 28–86 %

claims.claim: field: Murphy Flowage's heavy, unlimited fishery took 2–12 % of its panfish a year
claims.source_value: panfish angling exploitation 2–18 % (bullhead 2, yellow perch 5, pumpkinseed 8, black crappie 11, bluegill 12, rock bass 18; mean 9 %); pressure was 'about average' for north-central waters, not heavy; 'unlimited' (no season, bag or size limits) is right

notes: Every paper value checks; the citation needs completing, the OCR caveat in §3.7.6 can go, and the code's 'heavy … 2–12 %' should be 'about average … 2–18 %'. Other useful values: total annual mortality 57 % for all species, panfish and game fish alike; natural mortality averaged 46 % for panfish, 30 % for game fish; estimated natural mortality in the absence of fishing 49 % (all species); 1.88 fish an hour; winter (ice) catch 4.2 fish/h vs 1.6 in summer; the 10 % most successful anglers took 50 % of the fish; bass exploitation rose in 1968–69 with a crayfish decline and a winter drawdown that reduced vegetation (Snow 1971).
